browser: User Chrome 153, existing five-book overview tab
method: CDP Performance.getMetrics deltas, no navigation or app code changes. ProcessTime delta / Timestamp delta reports one-core-equivalent CPU, not whole-machine utilization. Existing All Works panel pauses Canvas for the control condition.

findings: Sustained visible-idle CPU reproduced twice; pausing scene through existing panel reduced renderer process CPU by approximately 97%.
Scene.jsx Canvas runs always while visible and no panel is open. Hearth, particles and table animation continue in idle overview.
Two point-light shadow maps and multisampling/Bloom/Vignette execute within the continuous render pipeline. Individual cost was not isolated.
SoftBook.mjs updateSoftBook skips geometry recalculation for unchanged time; idle closed-book geometry recalculation hypothesis is not supported.
Visibility listener already switches hidden page to demand. This diagnosis concerns a visible idle page, not proof of hidden-tab continuous rendering.
Other busy host processes were observed; their resource usage is not attributed to this page. GPU-specific utilization and memory leakage were not measured.
limitations: Profiler.enable was unavailable through the browser capability; five-second awaited evaluation exceeded its three-second command timeout, then a 1.8-second read-only RAF sample succeeded. No CPU call-stack profile or individual-pass ablation was obtained.
recommendation: Next optimization: cache unchanged point-light shadow maps with correct dynamic invalidation; measure before/after. Consider lower idle animation cadence separately while preserving full interaction/opening cadence and approved appearance.
